mine_p04_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_001.text: On Day 458, Zeng Bo waited outside the mine office with an empty tool roll beneath his arm. He had come twice since the evening complaint at Han's lodging house. His repaired hammer remained in the outer receiving store, while a supplier's larger shipment had crossed into ordinary use. He did not claim the two deliveries had identical terms. He claimed nobody had explained why his own small tool seemed able to wait forever. Lin arrived for her issued surface half-day and found his anger occupying the doorway before she reached it.

mine_p04_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_002.text: Qiao asked him to step aside so the lamp attendants could pass. Zeng moved but kept speaking. The hammer was his, he said. Its head had belonged to his father, its handle had been replaced many times, and a workshop had just completed the new repair he had paid for. He had expected to use it for private carpentry after his mine shifts. The company issued tools for assigned mine work. It had not agreed to replace the income his own hammer could earn elsewhere.

mine_p04_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_003.text: The forewoman asked which receiving record held it. Zeng gave the bundle number from memory and then produced the actual paper. His fingers shook enough to make the folded corner difficult to open. Lin offered a clean place on the side table. He put the sheet there himself. Its heading named the surface store. Beneath that heading, an owner field read Mine Stores. Zeng struck the incorrect words with one finger. He had brought a complaint about a delay and found himself needing to prove that his father's hammer had not become company stock.

mine_p04_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_004.text: The supplier's local steward, Sui Jun, came from the cargo bay with red dust along the hem of his coat. He had not packed the tool bundle. His instruction required a valid owner comparison before release from the receiving store. If he handed a wrongly identified object to the first angry person who described it, another owner might bear the loss. Zeng called that answer convenient. Sui said the store did not improve its position by keeping an ordinary hammer nobody there could legitimately use.

mine_p04_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_005.text: Lin saw the space between their statements and knew enough not to close it with her own confidence. The owner field was wrong if Zeng's account was correct. Sui's release instruction still required a comparison. Qiao asked Ren to fetch the receiving references which each responsible holder could actually supply. They would examine those before making a title or payment decision. Zeng wanted his tool now. The words before making sounded like another locked door, and he turned his back on the table.

mine_p04_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_006.text: A passing worker told him to let the cultivator speak. Lin felt the invitation become pressure before she answered it. She could supply an observation from the permitted public records she knew, if useful. She could not order a store opened or identify an unseen hammer with spiritual certainty. Zeng looked at her dull practice sword and then away. He had not asked for a mountain-splitting champion. He wanted somebody who would remain in the room long enough for a small claimant's papers to be read.

mine_p04_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_007.text: Her issued mine half-day did not include representing him. Qiao assigned her the already agreed public board task and named another clerk for the receiving inquiry. Lin completed her duty first. Watching an upsetting event did not erase the task another person had paid her to do, nor could she bill the same hours twice. At the agreed end she returned the board and asked Zeng whether he wanted a conversation afterward. He said yes, then apologized for answering as though she had already refused.

mine_p04_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_008.text: They sat outside on the low wall. Zeng unrolled the tool cloth although the hammer was absent. A square of lighter fabric marked where its head usually rested. He said his father had made a habit of putting every tool away before supper, even if it meant carrying one back across a room after the food was served. As a boy, Zeng had thought it a foolish ceremony. Now he remembered the movement of his father's hand more clearly than some of the things the man had said.

mine_p04_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_009.text: Lin asked whether the repair had altered a maker's mark. Zeng said the head was unchanged; only the worn handle had been replaced. The old handle had split along a grain he knew well. He had kept it because throwing it away felt different from replacing it. The new handle did not make the hammer somebody else's, and the old one did not remain safe because it held a memory. He laughed once at himself. Lin recognized the effort required to say both things without being given a moral lesson about letting go.

mine_p04_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_010.text: His repair agreement priced the ordinary work at six coppers, paid on completion. The workshop had issued a receipt. The mine receiving bundle combined several deliveries, and the outer label appeared to have carried the store destination into the owner field. Zeng did not know whether the error began at dispatch or receiving. Sui had found an unmatched entry and stopped release. Lin read the papers Zeng permitted her to see. She could already see one plausible path to the mistake, and plausibility was still not its proof.

mine_p04_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_011.text: The hammer's delay had affected two private jobs. One customer needed a window fastening repaired before a journey; another wanted a crate handle ready for market. Their gross quoted prices were not the same as Zeng's lost profit, and one job had not been finally accepted. He had written both as lost wages in his first complaint. Lin asked whether he wanted to preserve the distinction. He rubbed his face and said yes. Anger had made him write the largest figure he could honestly remember, rather than the precise kind of loss it represented.

mine_p04_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_012.text: He disliked correcting his own claim while the store still held the tool. Lin said a smaller supported account might be more answerable than a larger blurred one. Zeng asked whether she would say that to the supplier too. She said she would question any unsupported comparison she was actually asked and permitted to examine. He listened, then folded the job papers separately from the repair receipt. The act did not calm him. It gave his anger different pages to inhabit.

mine_p04_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_013.text: That afternoon, Sui obtained the workshop's duplicate repair receipt through the proper holder. The workshop confirmed the paid six-copper repair, the unchanged hammer head and Zeng's ownership instruction. Its dispatch note named the receiving store as destination. Another part of the bundle record still needed comparison with the mine's receiving copy. Qiao arranged an ordinary viewing interval where Zeng could identify his own property without entering the store unescorted. The appointment would not settle an expense claim before its actual sources were examined.

mine_p04_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_014.text: Zeng almost refused the viewing interval because it sounded like permission to visit what already belonged to him. Lin understood the insult he heard and the limited purpose the appointment actually served. She did not ask him to be grateful. Sui said the interval was the fastest safe comparison he could authorize under the current instruction. Zeng accepted it in writing. His acceptance did not waive the delay account. Qiao made that clear before any signature was taken, and he finally put the tool roll on the table.

mine_p04_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_015.text: At the surface store, the ordinary custodian opened the designated shelf. Lin attended only at Zeng's invitation and within the visitor condition. The hammer lay wrapped beside two mine-owned wedges. Zeng recognized the worn mark beneath its head. He asked to turn it, and the custodian permitted that light identification movement. The new handle's pale wood made the old metal look darker. Zeng held it without swinging. For a moment the object was unmistakably itself, and the paperwork still needed to catch up.

mine_p04_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_016.text: The custodian compared the maker mark with the workshop's retained image and Zeng's earlier owned-tool issue reference. Both supported the identification. The combined bundle's owner field had been copied from the destination heading during receiving. Ren found the copying line and its issuer. Nobody needed an echo from Zeng's father to establish the transfer error. The living worker's records and the ordinary object were enough. Sui asked for the authorized correction so the release could proceed without leaving the store's own register falsely stating that mine property had vanished.

mine_p04_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_017.text: The issuer, a tired receiving assistant named Fu Jie, came to the table after finishing an active cargo count. He had copied the wrong heading while several bundled parcels arrived at once. He admitted that error and disputed a rumor that he had been trying to acquire Zeng's tool. The supported mistake did not prove intentional theft. Zeng had heard the rumor himself and did not repeat it after Fu spoke. He wanted responsibility for the actual delay. A larger accusation would have made the receiving assistant defend an event nobody had established.

mine_p04_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_018.text: Fu's supervisor accepted the visible owner correction and retained the original entry beneath it. The hammer could be released after the completed comparison. Zeng still had questions about why a small parcel's mismatch had not been pursued earlier. Sui's large supplier shipment had received a scheduled comparator interval, while the unassigned tool question had waited for a clerk. Qiao acknowledged that difference in available process. The mine could not honestly answer the complaint by pretending every owner had found the same route through the receiving desk.

mine_p04_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_019.text: The forewoman proposed a posted correction contact and a response interval for unmatched personal tools. It would need staffing and a trial period, rather than a sentence placed on the wall and forgotten. Fu said he would welcome a way to refer mismatches before they became angry visitors. Sui wanted to know which source holders would be expected to respond. Zeng wanted a deadline that meant something to a person missing a paid job. The discussion grew sharper as soon as each person stopped speaking in generalities.

mine_p04_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_020.text: Lin had not yet accepted any representation role. Zeng asked whether she would help present his supported account, privately or through a public process if he consented to the particular details. He would not authorize publication of family recollections or other customers' names. She could also decline and provide only her own allowed observation. He would still submit his claim. The choice belonged to the help she might undertake, not to whether Zeng deserved an answer. Lin considered the work against her own appointments and the pressure of being useful.

mine_p04_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_021.text: Zeng invited Lin to his family's room on the evening before he expected her answer. He said his wife wanted to meet the person who had bothered to listen, and then seemed embarrassed by the pressure that invitation might create. Lin accepted supper as private company, not payment for taking the case. She brought a small bundle of greens bought from her own purse. At the door, Tao Mei took them and asked him to stop explaining the entire dispute before the guest had removed her muddy shoes.

mine_p04_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_022.text: Their daughter, Lan, had laid three places at the table although four people were there. She laughed at her mistake and fetched another bowl. The room contained a narrow bed, a stool with an uneven leg and a shelf crowded with objects somebody kept meaning to mend. Zeng's old hammer handle lay beside the window. Lin could see its split without picking it up. Tao asked if she wanted hot water on her cold hands. For a moment, care had a simple shape and no form to complete.

mine_p04_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_023.text: During supper Zeng began describing the ownership error again. Tao interrupted him to ask whether he wanted another cake. He answered the other question, then noticed and smiled reluctantly. She said she had heard the error often enough to recite it and still wanted him to eat while the food was warm. Lin watched affection interrupt an argument without denying that its cause remained. A delayed tool had entered every evening in the room, and the people living there needed something besides the delayed tool.

mine_p04_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_024.text: Lan asked whether the new hammer handle would remember her grandfather. Zeng said wood did not remember him in the way people did. The head still carried his ordinary maker's mark, and they could tell stories with either handle beside them. His father had died after an ordinary illness three years earlier. No recorded echo waited in the hammer. Lan considered the answer, then said the old handle looked like a crooked flute. Zeng said it would make a terrible tune, and she demanded a demonstration.

mine_p04_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_025.text: He blew across one end and produced only an undignified breath. Lan laughed so hard that Tao took her bowl before the soup spilled. Lin laughed with them. The broken handle did not become useless grief or a magical surviving person. It was an unsafe old tool part which a family could keep for reasons that did not require loading it again. Zeng set it back beside the window. His absent father had occupied the room briefly through their own living conversation.

mine_p04_026.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_026.text: After supper Tao asked Lin about the dull sword. Lin described alignment practice with an ordinary blade. Zeng admitted he had once imagined that six paired routes meant she could simply lift the store's latch with her thoughts. She showed them her ordinary hand and said the latch belonged to an actual locked door. Tao said she preferred an answer which left the building standing. Lin liked the joke, then realized she had been relieved to be welcomed without being asked for an impressive demonstration.

mine_p04_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_027.text: Zeng's main mine wages had continued through work using issued tools. The held hammer affected his separate private carpentry and the plans tied to it. Tao did not want those differences lost. She had put money aside for Lan's winter clothing and did not wish a complaint to make their household sound either destitute or comfortably indifferent. Lin listened rather than borrowing the family budget as evidence. If Zeng chose a representation route, the claim could use the actual relevant loss under its agreed conditions.

mine_p04_028.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_028.text: Tao said the mine sometimes made a person shout before a small problem seemed large enough for a desk. Zeng said shouting had made Fu look afraid. He had not wanted that result, though he still wanted the receiving error answered. The room grew quiet. Lin asked whether he planned to correct the theft rumor if it returned. He said he would. Tao touched his sleeve. Responsibility could reach both directions without placing the same cause or burden on every person who had been angry.

mine_p04_029.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_029.text: Walking back to Han's lodging, Lin felt the offered supper tug at her decision. She had not promised to represent Zeng, and the family's kindness made refusal harder. She stopped beneath the repaired window awning and named that pressure to herself. It mattered because she wanted the eventual answer to remain one she could actually perform. A generous meal did not extend her days. She could choose a bounded role, or decline one, without declaring the people who had fed her manipulative for having been kind.

mine_p04_030.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_030.text: In the morning she reviewed her mine half-days, rest and the possible comparison dates before answering. She did not need a reserve test to decide whether a conversation belonged in the hours available to her. Zeng had supplied public and confidential consent options, not an unlimited request that she rescue his life. Lin returned to the surface office ready to choose the work she could honestly undertake and accept the consequences for what would remain outside it.

mine_p04_031.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_031.text: Sui asked whether a public account would expose the supplier's private workshop method. Zeng said his complaint concerned ownership, timing and access to a correction contact. The repaired handle's technique was not his evidence. Qiao kept that distinction in the proposed scope. Fu asked that any account identify the supported copying error without implying deliberate theft. Zeng agreed to the evidence boundary and retained his right to describe how the delay had affected him. A person could authorize scrutiny without surrendering every part of a private life.

mine_tool_choice.speaker: narrator
mine_tool_choice.text: Lin could help with a public bounded presentation, assist a confidential comparison, or leave representation with Zeng and contribute only her own permitted facts. The public route might support a correction service useful to other workers but would take more scheduled discussion. The private route could resolve his specific matter with less exposure and leave the broader practice less examined. Declining would protect her own available time and leave him seeking another helper. None of the choices would make the hammer hers or let her spend its owner’s rights as a personal resource.

choices.text: Help present Zeng's permitted ownership and delay account publicly.
Assist Zeng's confidential source comparison, keeping private terms closed.
Limit your contribution to allowed facts and leave representation with Zeng.

mine_tool_public.speaker: narrator
mine_tool_public.text: Lin accepted the public presentation under Zeng's stated consent. They first removed his father's private recollection and the customers' names from the copy set. The account retained the paid repair, owner misidentification, actual hold and supported delay effects. Zeng read every proposed public line. He changed one sentence which made him sound grateful for a viewing appointment. Lin kept his wording within the actual facts. Representing him would not mean replacing his voice with a more pleasing version of it.

mine_p04_public_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_002.text: The public discussion was booked for Day 460 outside Lin's mine half-day. Qiao named the staff who could answer the source questions, and Zeng invited another worker to accompany him. Fu attended with his supervisor. Sui brought the permitted receiving instruction rather than proprietary method papers. The room was small and warm. Lin read the sequence, then stopped so Zeng could describe the lost opportunity in his own limited terms. Several workers had expected a theft story and found themselves hearing something more ordinary and harder to dismiss.

mine_p04_public_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_003.text: Zeng distinguished the accepted private job from the unaccepted quotation. He did not ask the reviewer to treat both gross prices as net wages. The authorized reviewer would compare the supported loss and applicable obligations separately. Lin presented only the sequence she could substantiate. Qiao accepted that the unmatched personal-tool question lacked the response route given to larger booked shipments. The forewoman did not defend that difference by praising everyone's intentions. She asked which actual staffing change could keep a future mismatch from waiting unnoticed.

mine_p04_public_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_004.text: A lamp attendant described her own earlier difficulty recovering a privately owned wick trimmer from a combined bundle. She chose to submit the account through the new trial contact rather than have Lin add it to Zeng's case. Another worker wanted to complain about an unrelated price increase. Qiao directed that issue to its proper process. The public room did not become one enormous claim. Its useful consequence was a bounded correction contact with an assigned clerk and a stated reply interval for personal-tool mismatches.

mine_p04_public_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_005.text: The trial contact would operate twice weekly for six weeks under an allocated desk interval. It did not promise immediate release before ownership checks. It promised an acknowledged question, a named source request and a response date. Workers could see when a request had been received without reading another owner's private pages. Ren accepted the first interval. Fu's supervisor adjusted the receiving summary form so destination and owner could not be confused so readily. The changes used real staff time, which the forewoman entered in the work plan.

mine_p04_public_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_006.text: Zeng's hammer was released on Day 460 after the corrected source comparison and custodian receipt. He tested its new handle in the workshop's agreed ordinary way before using it for a paid task. The claim reviewer kept the delay question open for its scheduled disposition, separate from the completed property return. Lin did not call the whole matter finished because the tool roll looked full again. Zeng had his property and a public correction route; the supported expense question still had its own source work to complete.

mine_p04_public_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_007.text: Outside the office, he thanked Lin and then said he wished the meeting had not made him sweat so much. She admitted she had been afraid of reading his account in a voice too calm for his anger. He said the anger had reached the room anyway. They bought tea with their own money and sat where the steam would not wet the retained copy. The afternoon gave them a relationship which was not reducible to the successful return. Zeng could be relieved and still tired of explaining what had happened.

mine_p04_public_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_public_008.text: Qiao posted the bounded trial-contact notice after its staffing line was accepted. Lin read it from the surface lane the next morning. It did not name Zeng's family or the workshop's private method. It named a route a worker could use. The hammer's return had become one practical change in mine life, and people would later judge that change by whether the contact actually answered them. Lin had agreed to help make the account public. She had not agreed to become the contact herself whenever a worker found her eating supper.

mine_tool_private.speaker: narrator
mine_tool_private.text: Lin accepted the confidential comparison under Zeng's stated terms. They prepared the paid repair, owner references and supported delay account for the named reviewer. His father's recollection remained private, as did the other customers' identifying information. Zeng retained the originals and chose which permitted copies the reviewer could hold. Lin's role concerned this specific claim. It did not authorize her to tell the lodging table a dramatic version once the door closed behind them.

mine_p04_private_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_002.text: The comparison was booked for Day 460 outside Lin's mine half-day. Sui attended with the actual receiving instruction, and Fu came with his supervisor. Zeng brought the repaired-tool receipt and the private job terms relevant to his claim. The reviewer examined the owner error and asked separate questions about the hold and loss. Lin helped keep the source sequence clear. Nobody in the room needed to describe the workshop method or decide whether Zeng had been sufficiently polite while his tool waited.

mine_p04_private_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_003.text: The corrected ownership comparison supported release of the hammer. The reviewer also accepted the need to examine the response delay under the applicable arrangement. That question remained distinct from whether the receiving assistant intended theft, which the sources did not establish. Zeng said he had wanted an answer without becoming a public example. Lin heard the relief in that sentence. A confidential process had met one of his needs and would not automatically show other workers how to pursue a similar mismatch.

mine_p04_private_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_004.text: Sui agreed to revise his own local referral note so an unmatched personal-tool question reached the responsible source holder promptly. The revision belonged to the steward's accepted instruction and did not create a posted general service. Qiao was notified of the supported internal change without receiving Zeng's private job details. Lin could describe that an internal comparison occurred if Zeng allowed it. She could not expand the matter into a public worker account simply because a broader reform now seemed useful.

mine_p04_private_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_005.text: The hammer was released on Day 460 after the correction and custodian receipt. Zeng checked the new handle in the workshop's agreed ordinary way before using it. Lin returned the private comparison copies which were not authorized for her retention. The reviewer kept only the accepted claim set. A completed property return did not mean the supported delay-cost question had already received a disposition. Zeng wrote the next scheduled contact date inside his tool roll, where he would find it without carrying the whole folder to every job.

mine_p04_private_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_006.text: At the lodging house, somebody asked whether the supplier had finally admitted stealing the hammer. Zeng corrected the allegation himself. Lin did not disclose the confidential account to make her own contribution look impressive. She said the property question had been resolved through the permitted comparison and left the remaining details with their holders. The questioner disliked the short answer. It was not the answer a satisfying rumor wanted. Zeng drank his soup and appeared grateful for the ordinary silence that followed.

mine_p04_private_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_007.text: Later he invited Lin to see the repaired tool at the surface workshop. Its new pale handle carried no maker's mark from his father. The old head still did. He used the hammer for a light ordinary test, then put it away before supper as his father had done. Lin watched without asking to touch it. His invitation was personal, not evidence for her future inquiry. The confidential choice had changed what others could know, and it had also made room for a friendship which did not begin with a public audience.

mine_p04_private_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_private_008.text: Qiao did not post a general personal-tool correction contact on the basis of this confidential claim. Sui's internal referral change remained available within his own work. Another worker with a similar problem would still need to find the responsible source route or seek a separately authorized public process. Lin accepted that limit rather than borrowing Zeng's private matter to obtain an outcome he had not chosen. The hammer's return was useful. Its quieter route left a different public workplace behind it.

mine_tool_pause.speaker: narrator
mine_tool_pause.text: Lin declined representation and offered only her own permitted observation of the public receiving sequence. Zeng looked disappointed and did not accuse her of owing more. He had asked for help and received a bounded answer. She gave him the relevant public reference without reading his private job terms further. Qiao directed him to the worker-appointed claim helper whose next interval was later that week. The alternative existed, but it would not erase the additional waiting time.

mine_p04_pause_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_002.text: Zeng accepted the later helper appointment on Day 462. The helper, Luo Bin, read the paid repair and owner sources with him under their own agreement. Lin remained at her accepted mine work during that interval and did not bill herself as part of it. She saw Zeng in the lane afterward carrying the same empty roll. He said the helper had understood the mistaken heading. That was progress, and his private customer had already assigned the urgent window task to someone else.

mine_p04_pause_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_003.text: The tool comparison reached the responsible source holders on Day 465. Fu acknowledged the owner-field copying error, and Sui supplied the release instruction through the reviewer. Zeng attended with Luo rather than Lin. When he later described the permitted public outcome to her, she recorded only what he allowed and what the issued notice confirmed. She had chosen not to represent him. That choice could not become invisible by appropriating another helper's completed work as part of her own mine story.

mine_p04_pause_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_004.text: The hammer was released on Day 466 after the corrected comparison and custodian receipt. Zeng checked its new handle before paid use. The supported delay account remained with his claim helper and the authorized reviewer. The return happened later than the earlier offered comparison could have occurred. One accepted private task had gone elsewhere while he waited. Lin could regret that consequence without claiming she had caused every part of the store's error or pretending her own appointments made the lost opportunity unreal.

mine_p04_pause_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_005.text: Sui corrected the particular receiving entry and reminded the source holders to separate destination from ownership. No general posted contact was created from Zeng's matter. Luo would submit a separate staffing request if Zeng and other workers wanted it. The hammer's return resolved an ordinary property problem through other people’s work. It did not produce a public service merely because Lin knew about the event. She kept the difference in her notes and the helper's name beside the actual comparison.

mine_p04_pause_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_006.text: At Han's supper table, Zeng sat farther from Lin for a few evenings. He was not punishing her with an announced rule. He had other people to speak with and an experience they had shared. Lin resisted asking him to reassure her that declining had been acceptable. She could protect her own time and still live with someone else's disappointment. The mine's relationships would not become effortless simply because she had made a defensible decision.

mine_p04_pause_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_007.text: On Day 468, Zeng greeted her while carrying the filled tool roll toward a new private repair. He said the window job was gone but the crate customer had accepted a later ordinary appointment. Lin wished him sound work. She did not ask for a share of the result because she had supplied a public reference. The greeting restored something modest between them, less intimate than a shared claim meeting and more honest than a friendship declared complete before its participants had lived through the delay.

mine_p04_pause_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_pause_008.text: Her own accepted work and rest intervals had remained intact. That mattered to the curriculum she intended to investigate later. It did not compensate Zeng or place his lost task on a cultivation ledger. Lin wrote the public outcome with Luo Bin's actual role and left private details unclaimed. The choice to limit her help had preserved one part of her life while leaving another person's problem to a slower available route. Both consequences would remain part of the mine she now knew.

mine_p04_after_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_001.text: By Day 468, the ordinary receiving store had corrected the hammer's owner field. The form's revised layout would keep destination and owner apart in future combined bundles. That change followed the verified copying error, regardless of who had represented Zeng. It would need use and checking to prove helpful. Lin watched Fu prepare the next bundle record without making him perform an apology for every passerby. Responsibility for a mistake could include better work instead of becoming a permanent public identity.

mine_p04_after_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_002.text: The mine's larger supplier deliveries continued under their own accepted appointments. Their size did not prove that every delay to a smaller owner's parcel was malicious. It did reveal how easily assigned process could become available to one kind of claimant and obscure to another. Qiao asked the work leads to identify who actually answered a mismatch. Sui named his supplier sources. Ren named the public receiving references. The list exposed a gap without pretending the forewoman could fill it by announcing that fairness had been achieved.

mine_p04_after_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_003.text: Lin completed the week's issued surface half-days and received the corresponding wage after performance was checked. She paid the agreed board from actual earnings and kept her own practice reserve separate. The hammer dispute had occupied free time differently according to the help she accepted. Her paid mine hours had not secretly expanded into all of it. She was tired in a way the weekly figures did not describe. A ledger could identify money; it could not tell her which conversation would follow her into sleep.

mine_p04_after_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_004.text: Fu Jie stopped Lin near the receiving table one afternoon and asked whether she thought he should leave the job. He had made other small errors and feared the next one would harm somebody more badly. Lin did not assess his whole future from one corrected heading. She asked whether he had spoken to his supervisor about workload and training. He said he had, awkwardly. The supervisor had assigned a second check for combined bundles during the trial period. Fu looked ashamed of needing it and relieved that it existed.

mine_p04_after_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_005.text: Lin told him she had needed somebody to correct a date she read from a timber board. He laughed without believing the mistakes had identical consequences. They did not. Her admission made it easier to discuss what a check was for. Fu wanted the second reader to catch an error before an owner lost time, rather than discover it later as proof that he had never deserved the desk. Lin went back to her own issued task. She could offer company without becoming his supervisor or examiner.

mine_p04_after_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_006.text: Sui Jun crossed the yard carrying a parcel too light to require a porter. He had taken it himself because the addressed clerk was finishing another task. Zeng watched him from the wash basin and did not apologize for having complained. Sui did not demand an apology. They exchanged a stiff greeting which would not satisfy a story seeking immediate friendship. Lin saw it from the public lane. A corrected record could make future work possible while the people involved still needed time to stop hearing the old argument in each other's voice.

mine_p04_after_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_007.text: The supplier steward later told Qiao that his office needed a named source contact at the mine for bundled personal property. He would otherwise keep receiving questions which required records he did not hold. Qiao said her own desk had the corresponding problem with workshop duplicates. Their disagreement concerned actual work and access. Each wanted the other organization to answer sooner. Lin prepared the permitted contact list under instruction, leaving the proposed response interval for the people who could allocate real staff time.

mine_p04_after_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_008.text: On a free afternoon, Lin visited the surface memorial board where the mine named workers who had died in earlier accidents. Lu Sen's name appeared among others. Dates and family-authorized words occupied less space than the rumors she had heard at supper. She read them without trying to hear a voice. A fresh flower lay beneath one line and had begun to wilt. Somebody living had brought it. The board asked no qi from her and offered no technique in return.

mine_p04_after_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_009.text: She remained there longer than she intended. The hill behind the board held an old spoil heap covered with coarse grass. A moth moved between two blades near the base, its wings grey in the ordinary light. Lin thought about the word living and the names carved above her. The distinction mattered without becoming a clever answer. A colony might survive in the mountain; a recording might retain Lu's song; people might still miss him. None of those facts would undo the death recorded on the board.

mine_p04_after_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_010.text: When she returned, Lei An had saved a small barley cake beside the household lamp cloths. Lin asked what occasion required generosity. Lei said the cake had broken and would not sell well at the stall. It tasted the same in two pieces. They ate it while watching the evening cart clear the gate. Lin told Lei she wanted to learn what the moths actually did near the warm stones. Lei said the wildlife observer would probably prefer that question to another visitor asking what prophecy the wings contained.

mine_p04_after_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_011.text: Lei An asked whether the mine had become less interesting now that Lin knew one tool could provoke several days of argument. Lin said it had become more difficult to imagine as one mysterious place. Lei laughed and said that was an improvement. His missing lamp-store delivery had arrived late because an ordinary cart axle needed repair. The delay was recorded and the next lamp-stock check adjusted. Lin heard another bounded explanation which did not offer a single villain for the week's inconveniences.

mine_p04_after_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_012.text: They walked toward the surface gardens after supper. A narrow strip of damp soil lay between old spoil heaps and the lodging fence. Somebody had coaxed beans up sticks there. Lei pointed to moths gathering above a warm stone near the wall. They looked like the small grey visitor Lin had seen on the gallery rail. Their motion differed from a loose ash flake. Lin stopped at the path edge and watched without collecting one. The mine's next interesting question began with living creatures doing something she did not yet understand.

mine_p04_after_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_013.text: The wildlife observer had placed a public request for permitted sightings near cleared routes. Lei knew where it stood and offered to show Lin the next morning. The request did not ask visitors to enter closed workings or disturb a colony. Lin could choose to make an ordinary observation when rested and outside her accepted work. She thought of the ticking called a seam's voice, Lu Sen's recorded song, and the moth's movement. Three things could occupy the same mountain without becoming the same explanation.

mine_p04_after_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p04_after_014.text: A cart sounded at the yard gate, and Lei stepped back before continuing his sentence. Lin moved with him. The driver had an ordinary load and the friends had a clear place to stand. For once the small interruption felt easier than the arguments of the week. It gave them a straightforward action: leave the working path open. When the cart passed, Lei resumed the story of a moth which had landed in the lamp-store attendant's soup. Lin laughed and listened, ready for a living creature to be inconvenient rather than prophetic.
